title: Tamil script-to-sound research reference
scope: The 12 traditional independent vowel letters, 18 traditional consonant letters, aytham, and selected marginal loan spellings. This is an orthography-linked broad IPA inventory, not an exhaustive set of Tamil speech phones, a pronunciation lexicon, acoustic labels, or a clinical scoring key.

notation.ipa: Broad phonemic or citation-form target in slashes; surface variants in brackets. The slash values are provisional for an orthographic row, not a claim of one-to-one letter-to-phoneme mapping.
notation.consonant_letter: Tamil consonant letters have an inherent /a/ unless followed by a vowel sign or pulli (்). The letter field is the base letter, not an isolated consonant sound.
notation.vowel_sign: An empty sign means the inherent /a/ after a consonant. Other signs combine with a consonant in Unicode logical order.
notation.diphthongs: ஐ and ஔ are traditional vowel letters; the IPA sequences here are broad approximations and are not one steady-state vowel each.

special_orthography.caution: Do not assign a universal /h/ phoneme. It has historical uses and can modify following consonants in foreign-sound spellings.
Conventional conjunct/cluster (க + ் + ஷ), not an extra core Tamil consonant phoneme.

cross_cutting_rules.note: Short versus long vowel duration matters; the same Tamil vowel letter has no automatic fixed millisecond target across children, rate, and context.
Consonant length/gemination must be represented in word-level pronunciations; it is not another set of 18 single-letter phonemes.
Stops can be voiced or weakened in context, so spelling alone cannot supply a single observed IPA sequence.
Literary, colloquial, regional, and code-mixed pronunciations can differ. A word lexicon must store approved variants with dialect/register tags.

before_model_use: Select the target Tamil register/dialect and the actual approved word list.
Have qualified Tamil linguists and speech-language clinicians review each word's permitted pronunciations and age-appropriate feedback.
Create a versioned word-to-IPA lexicon with context-specific variants; do not derive clinical error labels by simple grapheme lookup.
Validate any phoneme recognizer and error localization on consented, child-separated data; an adult reference bank is insufficient.
Do not connect this file to V1 scoring without an SSOT change-control decision and fail-closed tests.
